To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the Bayesian framework is proposed to recognize and quantify optimizer uncertainty; 2) UA-L2O is developed for the first time to estimate the posterior of optimizers; 3) UA-L2-O improves the uncertainty calibration and optimization performance; and 4) the proposed framework is applicable to a broad range of problems.
we introduce the novel Bayesian modeling and uncertainty quantification for L2O.
we introduce a Bayesian framework for learning to optimize, and the resulting uncertainty-aware L2Os are more accurate, more confident, and more robust than their counterparts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to model and quantitatively measure the uncertainty of the optimizer itself, which is a novel and promising perspective to improve the robustness and generalization of optimization.
the following questions: what, why, and how to model and quantize the optimizer uncertainty?
the uncertainty quantification of optimizers, with the hope to inspire future works to incorporate the algorithmic uncertainty for more robust optimization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the uncertainty of the optimizers is a new dimension of the optimization problem, and it is essential for the algorithmic design of the next generation optimizers.
UA-L2O can improve the accuracy and uncertainty of the optimization solution, and also the performance of the underlying optimization algorithm.
UA-L2O is able to improve the optimization performances and the posterior estimation, while the improvement is not necessarily monotonic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, we provide a new perspective for the uncertainty quantification of optimization algorithms, which can be further extended to the uncertainty-aware learning-to-optimize framework.

, UA-L3O provides a new angle to consider the optimization algorithm as a random variable, with a prior and a likelihood, and a posterior, which is the key to quantify the uncertainty of optimization.
, UA-L3O provides a principled and effective way for the uncertainty quantification and calibration of optimization algorithms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, the uncertainty of the optimizer is an important yet overlooked factor for optimization.
, the Bayesian perspective on L2O can help us better understand and model the uncertainty in algorithm design.
, the Bayesian framework is a promising direction to improve the optimization algorithm design and performance.
